r: Near Tallikota, between the **Krishna** and its tributary
**Sadasiva Raya** (nominal, last Tuluva); real power with regent **Aliya Rama Raya**, **son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya**
The "adventurous ruler" who **played one Sultan against another** until they united; marched with his brothers **Tirumala and Venkatadri**
**The Deccan Sultanates / combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda** – the **Bahmani kingdom** had already broken up
Local sources call the invading sultans the **'Pancha (Vancha) Padushas' (five sultans)**, falsely including **Akbar, the Delhi Padusha**
Rama Raya backed Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the **Raichur doab**
Sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel of Golconda
**Chand Bibi–Ali Adil Shah**, Bibi Jamal–Ibrahim Qutb Shah

Hampi **looted for about six months**; **Sewell** called it a "graveyard" (possibly exaggerated); Sadasiva and **Tirumala** fled to **Penukonda**; the empire's centre moved to the **Telugu country**; Nayakas grew autonomous
**Fourth** Vijayanagara dynasty; named after **Araviti (Aravidu)** village, **Kurnool** district
Founder, Rama Raya's brother; removed Sadasiva; crowned at Penukonda

Greatest and longest; "**Second Krishnadevaraya**", "**Second Andhra Bhoja**"; moved to Chandragiri; literary contests at **Venkatapati Vilasam**; **Vilapakam (1601)** and **Siddhavatam (1605)** inscriptions; Dutch at **Pulicat**; court scholar **Appayya Dikshita**; allowed Jesuit churches at **Nellore and Chandragiri**
Battle of **Toppur (1616)** – "second Talikota", won by **Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** and **Raghunatha of Tanjore**
**Madras** granted to **Francis Day** (1639) by **Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka** (Srikalahasti)
Last; defeated by **Bijapur** and Golconda (Vandavasi; Mir Jumla)
**Raja Wodeyar** took **Srirangapatna (1610)** and founded the Mysore kingdom under **Venkata II**

He named **Srirangaraya** successor; queen **Bayamma's adoption of a Brahmin boy** led to conspiracies under her brother **Gobbur Jaggaraju**; **Velugoti Yachamanayaka** backed Srirangaraya and Jaggaraju was finally defeated
**Krishnappa** made it independent c. 1565; **Tirumala Nayaka** (1623-59) built the **Tirumala Rayala Mahal**

2.x: **Chevvappa (Sevappa) Nayaka:** appointed ruler of **Thanjavur** by **Achyutaraya** in **1535 AD** (ruled 1535-1561); married **Murthamamba**, sister of Achyutaraya's queen; Thanjavur stayed **loyal to Vijayanagara** and was a fierce rival of **Madurai**.

r: Original name Varadayya; "Pada Kavita Pitamaha"; born at **Movva (Muvva), Krishna district**; padams with the mudra **Muvva Gopala**; sang for **Tirumala Nayaka of Madurai**, **Vijayaraghava Nayaka of Tanjore** and **Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda** (1500 padams dedicated to him)
Minister of the **Tanjore Nayaks** (Achyutappa, Raghunatha); wrote ***Sahitya Sudha***
Melted temple idols into cannon at **Gandikota (1657)**
Raya gopurams and kalyana mandapas spread through the Nayaka courts
Surveyed and mapped the ruins of **Hampi in 1800**; later the **first Surveyor General of India**
